notes: Twenty authored cases: eight clean/error pairs, two register variants, two style-only examples. Primary references checked by host; independent bilingual human review remains pending. No recordings, CEFR labels or calibrated scores. Do not pool v1 mood labels with v2.

cambridge_modals.rule: Core modal verbs take an infinitive without to; the following main verb is not inflected for the subject.

cambridge_present.rule: In ordinary affirmative present simple clauses, third-person singular subjects generally take the -s form.

treccani_agreement.rule: Italian articles and adjectives agree with their nouns in gender and number; verbs agree with their subjects in person and number.

crusca_register.rule: Subjunctive selection depends on construction and register; volere admits indicative as well as subjunctive in some contexts. A formal preference is not a universal grammar error.
